The curve starts from the origin and rises linearly with the electric field, reaching a drift velocity of 10^7 cm/s when the electric field is about 5 × 10^5 V/cm; after that, the curve becomes horizontal, indicating that the drift velocity remains constant. Reasoning: 1 μm = 10^-4 cm, so the electric field for 5 V applied over a 1 μm region is E = 5 / 10^-4 = 5 × 10^4 V/cm. The magnitude of the current density is J = q n v_d = (1.6 × 10^-19)(1 × 10^16)(10^6) = 1.6 × 10^3 A/cm^2 = 1.6 kA/cm^2.

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: it shows a straight-line drift-velocity dependence from (0,0) to (5 × 10^5 V/cm, 10^7 cm/s), followed by a constant region. From the text, compute the applied field across the 1 μm region: L = 1 μm = 10^-4 cm, so E = 5 V / 10^-4 cm = 5 × 10^4 V/cm. Since this is one-tenth of 5 × 10^5 V/cm, it lies in the linear part, so v_d = (1/10)(10^7) = 10^6 cm/s. Then calculate J = q n v_d = (1.6 × 10^-19)(1 × 10^16)(10^6) = 1.6 × 10^3 A/cm^2 = 1.6 kA/cm^2.
